answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties verify, with rewards vesting after a delay and being clawed back if later disputes reveal fraud. Creating a hundred meadow-colored identities does not multiply trust: each must separately obtain work, deliver useful results, and survive review before its stake unlocks. An attacker therefore pays the same real labor and locked capital per identity, while coordinated fake jobs risk losing the stake; the atlas of past verified outcomes makes reputation costly to counterfeit, even at dawn when new accounts appear.
